stimuli.text: Water enters a tank at a rate modeled by $$E(t) = 10 + 5\sin\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)$$ gallons per hour and leaves the tank at a rate modeled by $$L(t) = 7\sqrt{t + 1}$$ gallons per hour, for $$0 \leq t \leq 8$$. At time $$t = 0$$ the tank contains 88 gallons of water.

A particle moves in the xy-plane so that for $$0 \leq t \leq 3$$, $$\frac{dx}{dt} = 4\sin\left(\frac{t^2}{5}\right) + 0.5$$ and $$\frac{dy}{dt} = \cos(t)\,e^{t/4}$$. At $$t = 0$$ the particle is at $$(2, -1)$$.
People enter an amusement park at a rate modeled by a differentiable function $$P$$, where $$P(t)$$ is measured in people per minute and $$t$$ is measured in minutes. Selected values are shown.
Consider the differential equation $$\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x(y - 2)$$. Let $$y = f(x)$$ be the particular solution with $$f(1) = 0$$.
Consider the curve given by $$x^2 + xy + y^2 = 27$$.
A function $$f$$ has derivatives of all orders. Selected values are $$f(3) = 6$$, $$f'(3) = 2$$, $$f''(3) = -1$$ and $$f'''(3) = -6$$. For all $$x$$, $$|f^{(4)}(x)| \leq 30$$.

questions.stem: What is the average rate of change of $$H$$ over the interval $$0 \leq t \leq 7$$, in degrees Celsius per minute?

options.why: This is the average temperature, not the average rate of change.
This is the total change in temperature; it still needs to be divided by the elapsed time.
This divides time by temperature, which is upside down.

questions.explanation: Average rate of change $$= \frac{H(7) - H(0)}{7 - 0} = \frac{19 - 18}{7} = \frac{1}{7}$$ degrees per minute.

questions.stem: A curve is defined by $$x = t^{2} + t$$ and $$y = t^{3} - 3t$$. What is $$\frac{dy}{dx}$$ at $$t = 2$$?

options.why: This is $$\frac{dy}{dt}$$ alone.
Correct. $$\frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} = \frac{9}{5}$$.
This is $$\frac{dx/dt}{dy/dt}$$, upside down.
This divides second derivatives, which is not the slope.

questions.stem: What is $$\lim_{x \to 1} \frac{x^{2} + 2x - 3}{x - 1}$$?

options.why: The expression is undefined at the point, but its outputs nearby approach a single number, so the limit exists.
Correct. The numerator factors as $$(x - 1)(x + 3)$$. Cancel $$x - 1$$ and substitute: $$1 - (-3) = 4$$.
This adds the roots. After cancelling, the expression is $$x + 3$$, which approaches $$4$$.
Substituting gives $$\frac{0}{0}$$, an indeterminate form, not the value 0.

questions.explanation: Direct substitution gives $$\frac{0}{0}$$, so factor: $$x^{2} + 2x - 3 = (x - 1)(x + 3)$$. For $$x \neq 1$$ the expression equals $$x + 3$$, so the limit is $$1 - (-3) = 4$$.

questions.stem: A population satisfies $$\frac{dP}{dt} = 0.003P(200 - P)$$ with $$P(0) = 80$$. What is $$\lim_{t \to \infty} P(t)$$?

options.why: Logistic growth levels off; it does not grow without bound.
Correct. The carrying capacity: the factor $$(200 - P)$$ makes growth stop at $$P = 200$$.
This is where the population grows fastest, not its limit.
The population changes from its initial value; it is not constant.

questions.explanation: Since $$0 < P(0) < 200$$, $$\frac{dP}{dt} > 0$$ and $$P$$ increases toward the equilibrium $$P = 200$$.

questions.stem: A particle moves in the plane with $$x'(t) = \frac{8}{3}t$$ and $$y'(t) = \frac{5}{3}t^2$$. What is the speed of the particle at $$t = 3$$?

options.why: This is the slope of the path, not the speed.
This forgets the square root.
Speed is the magnitude of the velocity vector, not the sum of its components.

questions.explanation: At $$t = 3$$, $$\vec{v} = \langle 8, 15 \rangle$$, so the speed is $$\sqrt{64 + 225} = 17$$.

questions.stem: A twice-differentiable function $$f$$ satisfies $$f'(5) = 0$$ and $$f''(5) = 5$$. Which of the following must be true?

options.text: There is not enough information to classify $$x = 5$$.
options.why: The second derivative test applies because f″ ≠ 0.
Correct. f′ = 0 and f″ > 0: the graph is concave up at a horizontal tangent.
A maximum needs f″ < 0.

options.text: $$f$$ has a point of inflection at $$x = 5$$.
options.why: f″ is not zero, so this is not a candidate for inflection.

questions.explanation: By the Second Derivative Test, $$f'(c) = 0$$ with $$f''(c) > 0$$ gives a relative minimum.

questions.stem: What is $$\int_0^{2} \frac{1}{x + 2}\,dx$$?

options.why: This forgets to subtract the value at the lower limit.
Correct. $$\ln|x + 2|\Big|_0^{2} = \ln 4 - \ln 2 = \ln 2$$.
This uses a power-rule-style antiderivative; the antiderivative of 1/u is ln|u|.
This is the ratio minus one, not a logarithm.

questions.explanation: $$\int \frac{dx}{x + 2} = \ln|x + 2| + C$$, so the integral is $$\ln\frac{4}{2} = \ln 2$$.

questions.stem: What is the sum of $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} -\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^n$$?

options.why: Correct. Geometric with first term $$-\frac{1}{6}$$ and ratio $$\frac{1}{6}$$.
The first term depends on the starting index; check the term for the first value of n.
The formula is $$\frac{a}{1 - r}$$, not $$\frac{a}{1 + r}$$.
This divides by $$r$$ instead of $$1 - r$$.

questions.explanation: $$|r| = \left|\frac{1}{6}\right| < 1$$, so the series converges to $$\frac{-\frac{1}{6}}{1 - \left(\frac{1}{6}\right)} = -\frac{1}{5}$$.

options.why: Correct. The quotient rule gives $$f'(x) = \frac{2}{(-4x + 5)^2}$$, and at $$x = -1$$ the denominator is $$81$$.
This subtracts in the wrong order: the quotient rule is (bottom · top′ − top · bottom′) / bottom².
This divides the derivative of the numerator by the derivative of the denominator, which is not the quotient rule.
This forgets to square the denominator.

questions.stem: On which of the following intervals is the graph of $$f$$ concave down?

options.why: Correct. $$f'$$ is decreasing there, so $$f'' < 0$$.
Here f′ is increasing, so f is concave up. Concavity depends on whether f′ increases or decreases, not on the sign of f′.
Here f′ is increasing, so f is concave up. Concavity depends on whether f′ increases or decreases, not on the sign of f′.
Here f′ is increasing, so f is concave up. Concavity depends on whether f′ increases or decreases, not on the sign of f′.

questions.explanation: $$f$$ is concave down where $$f'$$ is decreasing, which on this graph means a segment sloping downward.

questions.stem: What is $$\int_0^{1} x\left(x^2 + 2\right)^{3}dx$$?

options.why: Correct. With $$u = x^2 + 2$$, $$du = 2x\,dx$$, the integral is $$\frac{1}{2}\int_{2}^{3} u^{3}\,du$$.
After substituting, the limits must change to u-values (from c to 1 + c), not stay 0 to 1.
This forgets the factor $$\frac{1}{2}$$ from $$du = 2x\,dx$$.
This evaluates only at the upper limit.

questions.stem: $$\int \left(5x^{4} + 2\cdot\frac{1}{x} + 5e^{x}\right)dx =$$

options.why: The antiderivative of 1/x is ln|x|, not a power of x.
This differentiates instead of antidifferentiating.
After raising the power, divide by the new exponent.
Correct. Raise the power by one and divide by the new power; the antiderivative of 1/x is ln|x|; e^x is its own antiderivative.

questions.explanation: Term by term: $$\int 5x^{4}dx = x^{5}$$, $$\int \frac{2}{x}dx = 2\ln|x|$$, and $$\int 5e^x dx = 5e^x$$. Add the constant of integration.

questions.stem: If $$\int_0^{4} f(x)\,dx = -6$$ and $$\int_0^{7} f(x)\,dx = 11$$, what is $$\int_{4}^{7} \left(4f(x) - 3\right)dx$$?

options.why: This adds the two given integrals; the integral from a to b is their difference.
This forgets to multiply the integral of $$f$$ by $$4$$.
The integral of the constant $$-3$$ over an interval of length $$3$$ is $$-9$$, not $$-3$$.

questions.explanation: $$\int_{4}^{7} f(x)\,dx = \int_0^{7} f - \int_0^{4} f = 17$$. By linearity, the requested integral is $$4 \cdot 17 + (-3) \cdot 3 = 59$$.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{x}{y}$$ with $$y(0) = 4$$?

options.why: This would have dy/dx = 1, which is not x/y.
Correct. $$y\,dy = x\,dx$$ gives $$y^2 = x^2 + C$$; $$C = 16$$, and the positive root matches $$y(0) = 4$$.
The initial value is positive, so the positive root is needed.
At $$x = 0$$ this gives $$\sqrt{4}$$, not $$4$$: the constant must be $$4^2$$.

questions.explanation: Separate: $$\int y\,dy = \int x\,dx$$, so $$\frac{y^2}{2} = \frac{x^2}{2} + C$$. With $$y(0) = 4$$, $$y^2 = x^2 + 16$$ and $$y = \sqrt{x^2 + 16}$$.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n}{\sqrt{n}}$$?

options.why: Correct. alternating series test, but p = 1/2 for the absolute values.
Not this one: alternating series test, but p = 1/2 for the absolute values.

options.text: It converges, but to a negative sum only if the first term is negative.
options.why: This statement is not a classification of convergence.
Not this one: alternating series test, but p = 1/2 for the absolute values.

questions.explanation: Test the absolute values first, then the series itself: alternating series test, but p = 1/2 for the absolute values.

questions.stem: The region enclosed by $$y = 2x$$ and $$y = x^2$$ is revolved about the x-axis. What is the volume of the resulting solid?

options.why: Correct. $$\pi\int_0^{2} \left[(2x)^2 - (x^2)^2\right]dx$$: outer radius squared minus inner radius squared.
This is π times the area of the region, not a volume of revolution.
This uses only the outer radius (a disc instead of a washer).
This squares the difference of the radii instead of taking the difference of the squares.

questions.stem: Let $$P_{4}(x)$$ be the degree-4 Taylor polynomial for $$f$$ about $$x = 1$$, and suppose $$|f^{(5)}(x)| \leq 30$$ for all $$x$$. What is the Lagrange error bound for $$|f(\frac{5}{2}) - P_{4}(\frac{5}{2})|$$?

options.why: The distance from the center must be raised to the power n + 1.
This forgets to divide by $$(n + 1)!$$.
This uses the degree n instead of n + 1 for the factorial and power.
Correct. $$\frac{30}{5!}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{5}$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = x^{3} + x - 2$$, and let $$g$$ be the inverse function of $$f$$. What is $$g'(8)$$?

options.why: This evaluates $$f'$$ at $$8$$ instead of at the input $$2$$ with $$f(2) = 8$$.
This is $$f'(2)$$; the inverse's derivative is its reciprocal.
This takes the reciprocal of a function value, not of the derivative.

questions.stem: An open-top box is made from a 6-inch by 6-inch square of cardboard by cutting equal squares of side $$x$$ from each corner and folding up the sides. What value of $$x$$ gives the box its maximum volume?

options.why: This is not a critical point of the volume.
This is not a critical point of the volume.
At this cut the base has zero width, which gives volume 0 (a minimum).

questions.explanation: $$V'(x) = (6 - 2x)^2 - 4x(6 - 2x) = (6 - 2x)(6 - 6x)$$. On $$0 < x < 3$$, the only critical point is $$x = 1$$, where $$V'$$ changes from positive to negative.

questions.stem: The sum of $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n^{2}}$$ is approximated by its first 3 terms. What is the smallest upper bound on the error given by the alternating series error bound?

options.why: This is the last term used, not the first one omitted.
The exponent stays the same as in the series.
Correct. The error is at most the first omitted term.
This skips a term: the bound is the very next term.

questions.explanation: The terms alternate, decrease in size and approach 0, so $$|S - S_{3}| \leq b_{4} = \frac{1}{4^{2}}$$.

questions.stem:
Which of the following series converge?

I. $$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^n$$

II. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$$

III. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n}$$

options.why: Correct. I: diverges (geometric with |r| = 5/4 ≥ 1). II: diverges (p-series with p = 1/2 ≤ 1). III: diverges (the harmonic series).
Check each series with an appropriate test: I diverges, II diverges, III diverges.
Check each series with an appropriate test: I diverges, II diverges, III diverges.
Check each series with an appropriate test: I diverges, II diverges, III diverges.

questions.explanation: Series I diverges: geometric with |r| = 5/4 ≥ 1. Series II diverges: p-series with p = 1/2 ≤ 1. Series III diverges: the harmonic series.

questions.stem: What is the least number of solutions that the equation $$f(x) = 0$$ must have on the interval $$[0, 4]$$?

options.why: This undercounts: each sign change between consecutive values guarantees its own zero.
Correct. The sign of $$f$$ changes 2 times between consecutive table values, and the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees a zero in each such interval.
The IVT only guarantees zeros where the sign changes; other zeros are possible but not required.
The IVT only guarantees zeros where the sign changes; other zeros are possible but not required.

questions.explanation: Because $$f$$ is continuous, the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees a solution of $$f(x) = 0$$ on every interval where the values change sign. Counting the sign changes in the table gives 2.

questions.stem: What is the radius of convergence of $$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{n\,(x + 1)^n}{3^n}$$?

options.why: The center is not the radius.
The series converges for all x only when the ratio limit is 0 for every x.
Correct. The ratio test gives $$\frac{|x + 1|}{3} < 1$$.
The radius is the reciprocal of this.

questions.explanation: $$\left|\frac{(n + 1)(x + 1)^{n+1}}{3^{n+1}}\cdot\frac{3^n}{n(x + 1)^n}\right| = \frac{n + 1}{n}\cdot\frac{|x + 1|}{3} \to \frac{|x + 1|}{3}$$. Convergence needs this below 1, so $$R = 3$$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $$\int_{0}^{4} f(x)\,dx$$?

options.why: Correct. Add the areas above the x-axis and subtract the areas below it.
Sign error: regions above the axis count positive.
This is the total area, treating regions below the axis as positive.
This is f(b) − f(a), the change in f, not the integral of f.

questions.explanation: Split $$[0, 4]$$ into unit intervals and add the signed areas of the trapezoids and triangles: the result is $$-5$$.

questions.stem: What is $$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\ln(1 + 6x)}{2x}$$?

options.why: This leaves out the chain-rule factor when differentiating the numerator.
$$\frac{0}{0}$$ is indeterminate; it does not mean the limit is 0.
Correct. The limit has the form $$\frac{0}{0}$$, so L'Hospital's Rule applies: $$\frac{6/(1 + 6x)}{2}$$.
This differentiates the numerator and denominator but then inverts the ratio, or applies the rule incorrectly.

questions.explanation: Direct substitution gives $$\frac{0}{0}$$. Differentiate the numerator and denominator separately (L'Hospital's Rule): $$\frac{6/(1 + 6x)}{2}$$, which gives $$3$$.

questions.stem: The region bounded by $$y = x^2$$, the x-axis, and the line $$x = 2$$ is revolved about the x-axis. What is the volume of the resulting solid?

options.why: The disc method has a factor of $$\pi$$.
$$(x^2)^2 = x^4$$, whose antiderivative is $$\frac{x^5}{5}$$.
This integrates the radius instead of the radius squared.

questions.stem: A function $$f$$ has $$f(-2) = 4$$, $$f'(-2) = 5$$ and $$f''(-2) = -4$$. Using the second-degree Taylor polynomial for $$f$$ about $$x = -2$$, what is the approximation of $$f(-1.9)$$?

options.why: The quadratic term must use $$(x - a)^2$$, not $$(x - a)$$.
This is the tangent-line (first-degree) approximation.
This forgets to divide the second derivative by $$2!$$.

questions.stem: A 13-foot ladder leans against a vertical wall. The bottom of the ladder slides away from the wall at a constant rate of 3 feet per second. How fast is the top of the ladder moving, in feet per second, when the bottom is 12 feet from the wall?

options.why: The top slides down, so its rate is negative.
This swaps the roles of x and y.
Correct. $$x^2 + y^2 = 169$$ gives $$x\frac{dx}{dt} + y\frac{dy}{dt} = 0$$. With $$x = 12$$, $$y = 5$$, $$\frac{dy}{dt} = -\frac{12(3)}{5}$$.
The two ends do not move at the same speed; their rates depend on the position.

questions.explanation: Let $$x$$ be the distance from the wall and $$y$$ the height. $$2x x' + 2y y' = 0$$, so $$y' = -\frac{x x'}{y} = -\frac{12 \cdot 3}{5} = -\frac{36}{5}$$ feet per second (the top is moving down).

questions.stem: For the curve $$x^2 + xy + y^2 = 7$$, what is $$\frac{dy}{dx}$$ at the point $$(2, -3)$$?

options.why: Sign error when solving for dy/dx.
This ignores the $$xy$$ term entirely.
This differentiates $$xy$$ as $$y$$, forgetting the product rule term $$x\frac{dy}{dx}$$.
Correct. $$2x + y + x\frac{dy}{dx} + 2y\frac{dy}{dx} = 0$$, so $$\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{2x + y}{x + 2y}$$.

questions.explanation: Implicit differentiation with the product rule on $$xy$$: $$2x + (y + xy') + 2yy' = 0$$. Solving, $$y' = -\frac{2x + y}{x + 2y}$$; at $$(2, -3)$$, $$y' = \frac{1}{4}$$.

questions.stem: For the curve $$x = t^2$$, $$y = t^{3} - 2t$$, what is $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$$ at $$t = 1$$?

options.why: This forgets to divide by $$\frac{dx}{dt}$$.
Correct. Differentiate $$\frac{dy}{dx}$$ with respect to $$t$$, then divide by $$\frac{dx}{dt} = 2t$$.
This divides $$y''(t)$$ by $$x''(t)$$, which is not the second derivative.
This is $$\frac{dy}{dx}$$, the first derivative.

questions.explanation: $$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3t^2 - 2}{2t} = \frac{3t}{2} - \frac{2}{2t}$$. Its $$t$$-derivative is $$\frac{3}{2} + \frac{2}{2t^2}$$, which is $$\frac{5}{2}$$ at $$t = 1$$. Dividing by $$2t = 2$$ gives $$\frac{5}{4}$$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $$\int_{0}^{1} \sqrt{1 + x^3}\,dx$$?

options.why: This is the change in the integrand, not the integral.
This integrates over only half of the interval.
This is a single rectangle using the right endpoint, a rough estimate rather than the integral.
Correct. Use the calculator's numerical integration.

questions.explanation: On a graphing calculator, $$\int_{0}^{1} \sqrt{1 + x^3}\,dx \approx 1.111$$.

questions.stem: Let $$y = f(x)$$ be the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = x + y$$ with $$f(2) = 1$$. Using the tangent line at $$x = 2$$, what is the approximation of $$f(2.1)$$?

options.why: Sign error in the step.
This is only the estimated change; add it to f(a).
This adds the slope without multiplying by the step 0.1.

questions.explanation: At $$(2, 1)$$, $$\frac{dy}{dx} = 3$$. The tangent line gives $$f(2.1) \approx 1 + 3(0.1) = 1.3$$.

questions.stem: Sand is added to a pile at a rate modeled by $$R(t) = 24 + 4\sin\left(\frac{t}{9}\right)\sqrt{t + 1}$$ cubic feet per hour, for $$0 \leq t \leq 7$$. At time $$t = 0$$ the pile contains 67 cubic feet of sand. How much sand is in the pile at $$t = 7$$?

options.why: This assumes the rate stays at R(T) for the whole time.
Correct. $$67 + \int_0^{7} R(t)\,dt$$.
This adds the rate at one instant, not the accumulated amount.
This is only the sand added; include the initial amount.

questions.explanation: Amount = initial amount + accumulated change = $$67 + \int_0^{7} R(t)\,dt \approx 67 + 192.220 = 259.220$$ cubic feet.

questions.stem: The temperature of a room, in degrees Fahrenheit, is modeled by $$H(t) = 86 + 9\sin\left(\frac{t}{6}\right)e^{-t/20}$$, where $$t$$ is measured in hours. What is the instantaneous rate of change of the temperature at $$t = 6$$, in degrees Fahrenheit per hour?

options.why: Correct. The calculator's numerical derivative of $$H$$ at $$t = 6$$ gives 0.320; the temperature is increasing.
This multiplies the rate by the time, which is not a rate.
This is the temperature itself, not its rate of change.
This is the average rate of change over $$0 \leq t \leq 6$$, not the instantaneous rate.

questions.explanation: The instantaneous rate of change is $$H'(6) \approx 0.320$$ degrees Fahrenheit per hour, from the calculator's numerical derivative.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \frac{e^{x}}{1 + x^2}$$. What is the value of $$f'(0.5)$$?

options.why: This divides the derivatives of the numerator and denominator instead of using the quotient rule.
This is the function value, not the derivative.
Correct. Use the calculator's numerical derivative (or the correct rule) at the given input.
This is the derivative at $$x = 1.5$$, not at $$x = 0.5$$.

questions.explanation: On a graphing calculator, evaluate $$\left.\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{e^{x}}{1 + x^2}\right)\right|_{x = 0.5} \approx 0.264$$.

questions.stem: What is the interval of convergence of $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(x + 2)^n}{n\cdot 5^n}$$?

options.why: The left endpoint gives $$\sum \frac{(-1)^n}{n}$$, which converges.
The radius is 5, from the factor $$5^n$$.
The endpoints are reversed: the right endpoint gives the divergent harmonic series.
Correct. Ratio test gives $$|x + 2| < 5$$; the left endpoint gives an alternating harmonic series (converges), the right endpoint the harmonic series (diverges).

questions.explanation: Ratio: $$\left|\frac{(x + 2)^{n+1}}{(n + 1)5^{n+1}}\cdot\frac{n\,5^n}{(x + 2)^n}\right| \to \frac{|x + 2|}{5}$$, so $$|x + 2| < 5$$. At $$x = 3$$: $$\sum \frac{1}{n}$$ diverges. At $$x = -7$$: $$\sum \frac{(-1)^n}{n}$$ converges.

questions.stem: A particle moves along a line with velocity $$v(t) = 3\sin(t)\,e^{-t/6} + 0.3$$. What is the total distance the particle travels over $$0 \leq t \leq 6$$?

options.why: This is the speed at the final time.
Correct. $$\int_0^{6} |v(t)|\,dt$$ on the calculator.
This is the average speed, not the distance.
This is the displacement; backward motion subtracts from it.

questions.explanation: Total distance $$= \int_0^{6} |v(t)|\,dt \approx 7.495$$. The displacement $$\int_0^{6} v(t)\,dt \approx 3.738$$ is smaller because the particle moves backward part of the time.

questions.stem:
Which of the following series converge?

I. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{2^n}{n!}$$

II. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n!}{3^n}$$

III. $$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^n$$

options.why: Check each series with an appropriate test: I converges, II diverges, III diverges.
Correct. I: converges (ratio test gives L = 0). II: diverges (ratio test gives L = ∞). III: diverges (geometric with |r| = 5/4 ≥ 1).
Check each series with an appropriate test: I converges, II diverges, III diverges.
Check each series with an appropriate test: I converges, II diverges, III diverges.

questions.explanation: Series I converges: ratio test gives L = 0. Series II diverges: ratio test gives L = ∞. Series III diverges: geometric with |r| = 5/4 ≥ 1.

questions.stem: What is the coefficient of $$x^{4}$$ in the Maclaurin series for $$f(x) = e^{4x}$$?

options.why: Sign error: check the sign pattern of the series.
The denominator is $$n!$$, not $$n$$.
The constant must be raised to the same power as x.
Correct. Substitute into the known Maclaurin series.

questions.explanation: Replace $$x$$ by $$4x$$ in the series for $$e^x$$: the $$x^{4}$$ term is $$\frac{(4x)^{4}}{4!}$$, so the coefficient is $$\frac{32}{3}$$.

questions.stem: A particle moves in the plane with $$x'(t) = \cos\left(\frac{t^2}{2}\right)$$ and $$y'(t) = e^{t/2}$$. What is the total distance the particle travels from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 1$$?

options.why: This adds the component displacements instead of integrating the speed.
Correct. Integrate the speed $$\sqrt{x'(t)^2 + y'(t)^2}$$.
This is the straight-line distance between the start and end points.
This is the speed at the final time.
The integrand must be evaluated at the upper limit, not at x.
Correct. By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus with the chain rule, substitute the upper limit and multiply by its derivative.
This leaves out the derivative of the upper limit, $$3x^{2}$$.
This evaluates the integrand at both limits; the derivative of an accumulation function only uses the variable limit.

questions.stem: What is the length of the curve $$y = e^{2x}$$ from $$x = 0$$ to $$x = 1.5$$?

options.why: This squares the function instead of the derivative.
Correct. $$\int_{0}^{1.5} \sqrt{1 + \left(2e^{2x}\right)^2}\,dx$$ on the calculator.
This is only the vertical change.
This is the straight-line distance between the endpoints, which is shorter than the curve.

questions.stem: What is the absolute maximum value of $$f(x) = x^2e^{-x/3} + \frac{\sin x}{4}$$ on the interval $$[0, 9]$$?

options.why: This is where the maximum occurs (the x-value), not the maximum value.
This evaluates f at the critical point of the first term alone; the sine term shifts the maximum.
Correct. Graph f on the calculator and find its maximum on the interval, checking the endpoints too.
